onsite

Bring-up for autonomous vehicle build, including troubleshooting, software testing, and verification.
Develop and implement test plans for routine software releases and changes, including both on-vehicle and simulation testing.
Evaluate the performance of different AV components, such as sensors, actuators, and algorithms, to ensure they meet safety and performance requirements.
Investigate and debug issues found during testing, working with other engineers to resolve problems and improve system performance.
Collaborate with other engineers, including software, hardware, and systems engineers, to ensure seamless integration and performance of AV systems.
Integrate software and hardware components, ensuring proper functionality and performance within the overall vehicle system.

M.S. or Ph.D. in automotive engineering, computer engineering, electronics/electrical engineering, or a related field.

Experience developing for and operating in a Linux Environment

At Bristol Myers Squibb, our employees often ask, “Who are you working for?”—a question that fuels collaboration, accountability, and urgency in our work. Our purpose-driven culture inspires us to discover, develop, and deliver innovative medicines to prevail over serious diseases. We offer uniquely interesting and meaningful work, opportunities for growth, and a supportive environment that values inclusion, wellbeing, flexibility, and comprehensive benefits. This is work that transforms the lives of patients, and the careers of those who do it.
Position Summary
The PDS BI&T team (Product Development & Supply Business Insights & Technology) partners with the BMS PDS organization to answer key business questions that drive supply strategy and operational decisions using data science, machine learning and Generative AI.
The Data Scientist, Sr. Specialist joins the Supply Risk Analytics team, reporting into the Risk Analytics lead, and contributes to AI-enabled analytics that quantify, monitor and mitigate risk across the BMS supply network and support network strategic decisions. This is a hands-on, early-career role with a clear growth path: you will work alongside experienced data scientists and engineers, take ownership of well-scoped pieces of larger solutions, and steadily build depth in supply risk analytics, probabilistic modeling and applied Generative AI. AI-assisted development is part of how the team works every day, and you will use Claude Code to build, test, document and refactor code from your first weeks.
The successful candidate has a quantitative background, solid Python and SQL fundamentals, curiosity about how AI is changing analytics work, and the communication skills to explain results to non-technical partners. Deep supply chain or life sciences knowledge is not required. We will teach you the domain.
What You Will Do
AI-Enabled Supply Risk Modeling:
Contribute to machine learning and probabilistic models, including Monte Carlo simulation, that quantify supply risk such as inventory-at-risk, service level exposure and supplier disruption scenarios, under the guidance of senior team members.
Help build Generative AI and agentic features using Claude: LLM-generated risk narratives, intelligent alerts, natural-language interfaces to risk data, and AI agents that automate scenario analysis.
Develop and maintain forecasting and anomaly detection components that produce risk scores and early-warning signals, and help translate outputs into clear recommendations.
Build interactive front-ends (e.g., Streamlit, React) that put risk models in the hands of business users, and create agentic workflows and reporting automations that replace manual, recurring analysis.
Balance quick-turn ad-hoc analyses for urgent business questions with long-running digital product development delivered in an agile setup of sprints, backlog refinement and retrospectives.
Document assumptions, data, methodology and validation results, applying BMS responsible AI, data privacy and quality practices.
Business Collaboration
Partner with Supply Chain, Business Continuity Management, Quality and Procurement stakeholders to understand priority risk questions and help frame them as analytic problems that support network strategic decisions.
Support demos and walkthroughs of results for business partners, growing toward presenting trade-offs to leaders independently.
Collaborate day to day with a cross-functional team of data scientists, engineers and business partners spread across the US, Europe and Asia, working effectively across time zones.
Engineering & Technology
Use Claude Code daily as a core development tool for scaffolding pipelines and models, generating tests, and refactoring and documenting code, while learning to apply sound engineering judgment and peer review.
Work with Data Engineering to define data requirements and build pipelines on Databricks and AWS Glue, ensuring model inputs are reliable and traceable.
Develop and deploy AI applications within BMS’s enterprise AI platform, learning to work in large, shared GitHub codebases with branching, code review, release and CI/CD conventions.
Write clean, reusable, well-tested Python and SQL, contribute to shared prompt libraries and components, and participate in agile ceremonies.
Actively seek feedback and coaching from the Risk Analytics lead and senior peers to grow in both data science and applied AI development.
Qualifications & Experience
Required Qualifications:
B.S. or M.S. in a relevant life sciences, informatics, data, or technical discipline (e.g., data science, statistics, operations research, engineering, computer science); advanced degree a plus.
2 - 4 years of experience in IT, informatics, data analysis, business analysis, or a scientific data-focused role; relevant graduate research or internship experience may be considered.
Working proficiency in Python and SQL for data manipulation, analysis and modeling, with a solid grounding in statistics and probability.
Some hands-on exposure to machine learning or Generative AI through work, coursework or personal projects, and a strong interest in AI-assisted development tools such as Claude Code.
Clear written and verbal communication and a collaborative, learning-oriented mindset, comfortable working in a global team across continents and time zones.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience with Databricks (Spark, Delta Lake, notebooks) or AWS data services such as AWS Glue.
Exposure to LLM application development (prompt engineering, RAG, LangChain/LangGraph, Anthropic Claude) or to AI agent development.
Familiarity with simulation or decision analysis under uncertainty (e.g., Monte Carlo methods).
Experience contributing to shared GitHub repositories, CI/CD tooling (e.g., GitHub Actions) and agile tools such as Jira.
Experience building analytic front-ends or visualizations (e.g., React, Streamlit).
Exposure to pharmaceutical supply chain, business continuity management or another

About the Role
We are looking for a Systems Performance Modeling Engineer to build the models and tools that predict how generative AI inference workloads perform on Tensordyne systems, from a single accelerator up through rack, pod, and cluster scale. This is a hands-on engineering role for someone who likes writing simulator code, running experiments, and digging into why a prediction and a measurement don't match.
Working closely with our architects and the silicon, hardware, networking, and software teams, you'll capture workload behavior, extend simulation and analytical models of our silicon, interconnect, and multi-hop fabrics, and validate them against real hardware. You'll be comfortable moving across the stack, from the model graph through collectives to the network fabric, to track down where performance is going.
What You'll Do
Implement and extend simulation-based performance models for multimodal generative AI inference at rack, pod, and cluster scale, covering compute, memory, collective communication, and network fabric.
Model how serving strategies (tensor, pipeline, and expert parallelism, prefill/decode disaggregation, batching, and KV-cache placement) interact with Tensordyne silicon and fabric topology, and measure the effect on latency, throughput, and cost per token.
Build trace-capture and replay tooling that records real execution from our inference runtime and replays it under hypothetical silicon, system, and network configurations.

About the Company
We are on a mission to bring human-like intelligence to robots.
We believe our workforce should focus on innovation and creativity; dull, dangerous, or dirty jobs should be left to robots. Our solution is powered by a type of Artificial Intelligence called Active Inference, letting robots learn resilient skills and adapt to situations they weren't explicitly trained for.
We’re a pre-Series A startup punching well above our weight, tripling our team since 2023 while building solutions for some of the world’s largest companies - including Fortune 20 customers and government contracts.
About the Team
We are a small, senior team [a varied mix of experience ranging from startups to Microsoft and Amazon], and we like working with people who came to robotics by unique and unusual routes.
We're dedicated to supporting new team members, and we care deeply about your career growth and personal development. We're a hybrid/remote team that values work-life balance, diverse perspectives, and learning from each other.
About the Job
You'll join the founding team building robotic arm systems. Enough work exists today that you won't start from a blank page; yet enough is missing that you'll own real pieces of it.
Four main areas, though they overlap more than the list suggests. Expect to work across them rather than inside one:
Motion planning
– computing collision-free paths through an environment.
Control
– executing those paths on real hardware, reliably.
Perception
– object detection and scene reconstruction.
Manipulation
– grasping and dexterous handling of objects.
You'll have people to collaborate with, including a team that answers questions, reviews your work, and shows up when something breaks. You'll be given direction, but not a detailed plan, as much of this is still unmapped. This position suits someone who takes ownership: finds the problem, solves it, and sees it through.
Job Responsibilities
Design, build, and maintain software that runs in both simulation and on real hardware.
Prototype fast to prove out ideas, then do the less glamorous half: hardening what works into systems that deploy and stay up.
Measure what the robot actually does: build the tests and metrics that catch regressions and close the gap between sim and reality.
Job Requirements
Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science or Engineering.
4+ years of relevant industry experience.
Domain knowledge of robotics such as Dynamics, Controls, Planning, Estimation, and Computer Vision.
Proficiency in Python.
Experience with C++, Git, ROS/ROS2, and Simulators (Mujoco, Gazebo, etc.).
Documentation and Communication Skills.
Due to the nature of this role working on US Government contracts, we're contractually obligated to hire a US Citizen or US Green Card holder for this position.
Nice to have
Real-time software & multithreaded systems.
3D math, linear algebra, embedded systems, signal processing.
Interest in Active Inference or Machine Learning.
Employee Benefits
12 paid holidays
Unlimited PTO, 2 week minimum
Flexible work hours policy
Hybrid/Remote work Schedule (CA/WA preferred)
100% Health, Dental and Vision coverage (Kaiser offered in CA)
Equity Incentive Package
$50/month for Health and Wellness

Veeam is the Data and AI Trust Company, specializing in helping organizations ensure their data and AI are fully understood, secured, and resilient to enable the acceleration of safe AI at scale. As the market leader in both data resilience and data security posture management, Veeam is built for the convergence of identity, data, security, and AI risk. Headquartered in Seattle with offices in more than 30 countries, Veeam protects over 550,000 customers worldwide, who trust Veeam to keep their businesses running. Join us as we go fearlessly forward together, growing, learning, and making a real impact for some of the world’s biggest brands.
Software Engineer, Veeam Data Cloud (FedRAMP)
We are looking for an experienced Software Engineer to join the Veeam Data Cloud (VDC) engineering team, working on the FedRAMP-compliant version of our SaaS product. The mission of the team is to build a secure, reliable, and easy-to-use data protection service that meets the bar federal customers hold us to — and to prove, in code and in tests, that it does. As a member of the team, you will design and build the microservices and security controls that make that compliance real.
This is an excellent opportunity for someone with cloud services and secure software development experience to help build the world's most successful, modern data protection platform. The ideal candidate will have held similar roles in a rapidly growing SaaS company.
This is not a compliance paperwork position — it's a software engineering role focused on cryptography, authentication, auditability, and the reliability of services running in production.
What You'll Do
Design and develop reliable, scalable microservices in Go and C#/.NET, integrated with cloud-based managed services.
Turn compliance requirements handed over by our compliance engineers into working application code — and the tests that prove the behavior holds.
Take FIPS-validated cryptography from requirement to running binary: build configuration, startup assertions, TLS mode enforcement, and CI checks a non-compliant build can't pass.
Instrument privileged operations with structured audit events — actor, target, before and after state, outcome, correlation ID — and wire them into the audit pipeline.
Harden authentication paths: OAuth client authentication with key pairs rather than shared secrets, stateless JWT validation via JWKS, and SAML federation through our identity provider.
Work across service API contracts and generated clients as services move onto private network paths.
Ensure your code is high-quality, thoroughly tested, and FedRAMP-compliant.
Participate in the on-call rotation for product operations.
Take ownership of the reliability and efficiency of your services running in the cloud.
Participate in technical design discussions, review code, and provide feedback to other engineers.
Collaborate with a distributed team — including compliance engineers who will bring you requirements and expect a clear answer on what the code actually does.
What You'll Bring
5+ years of experience in the software development industry.
Strong Go, or strong C#/.NET with real interest in working across both — most of the control plane is Go, and the Microsoft 365 services are .NET.
Demonstrated expertise designing, building, and running SaaS or large-scale cloud services on Azure, AWS, or GCP.
Working developer-level knowledge of applied cryptography and authentication: TLS, JWTs, OAuth/OIDC flows, key management. You don't need to be a cryptographer, but you should know what a JWKS endpoint is for and why a client secret is weaker than a signed assertion.
Experience with structured logging and observability — you've instrumented a service that someone else had to debug at 3am.
Expertise developing, testing, and debugging production-quality, scalable, concurrent systems.
Solid testing discipline, including tests that assert a security behavior rather than a feature.
Comfort reading a written requirement you didn't author, and asking the right clarifying questions before building.
A strong knowledge of computer science fundamentals (data structures and algorithms).
What You'll Get

Paid parental leave: 8 weeks for all parents, 16 weeks for birthing parents
Medical, dental, and vision coverage starting on your first day
Mental health support, therapy sessions, and digital wellness tools via our Employee Assistance Program
401(k) retirement plan with company matching contributions
Fertility, adoption, and surrogacy support through Maven, plus paid volunteer time
AirVet: 24/7 virtual veterinary care at no cost
Legal services, identity protection, and supplemental health insurance options
Tax-advantaged spending accounts for healthcare, dependent care, and commuting
Opportunities to learn and grow through on-demand libraries (LinkedIn Learning, O’Reilly), mentoring, workshops, and learning events like our annual Global Day of Learning

Robotics has a demo problem. GMR doesn't. Our systems are in active production today, adapting autonomously to real geometries, real materials, and real process variation without reprogramming. We deliver our system through a Robots-as-a-Service (RaaS) model that converts capital expenditure into an operating subscription, making Physical AI accessible to the manufacturers who need it most. We hire people who want to solve hard physical problems at an industrial scale.
The Role
GrayMatter Robotics runs physical robots at customer production sites, maintains a growing government enclave, and supports an engineering team that moves fast. Right now, too much of the IT work that keeps all of that running is falling on a DevOps engineer who should be focused on infrastructure, a QA engineer who shouldn't be configuring machines at all, and senior engineers who are getting pulled into IT requests they shouldn't have to touch.
We need one person to own that surface. Someone who can walk into an ambiguous IT situation, figure out what needs to happen, and drive it to resolution without needing to be managed through it.
That is the IT Systems Engineer. You will be the go-to for IT across the organization, covering internal infrastructure, fleet management, customer site support, and government enclave compliance. The role spans a wide range of domains on purpose. The right person is not a deep specialist. Who are Jack & Jill?
Ok, I'll go first. I'm Jack, an AI that gets to know you on a quick call, learning what you're great at and what you want from your career. Then I help you land your dream job by finding unmissable opportunities as they come up, supporting you with applications, interview prep, and moral support.
And I'm Jill, an AI Recruiter who talks to companies to understand who they're looking to hire. Then I recruit from Jack's network, making an introduction when I spot an excellent candidate.
How does this work?
Jack's an AI agent for job searching and career coaching. He works for you.
Jill is the AI recruiter working for the company. She recruits from Jack's network.
If it's a match and the company wants to meet you, they'll make the intro. In the meantime, if you'd like, Jack will send you excellent alternatives.
We never post fake jobs
This isn't a trick. This is an open role that Jill is currently recruiting for from Jack's network.

The rise of heavy-lift launch vehicles is shifting the industry from an era of mass constraint to one of mass abundance, and we believe this new era demands a fundamentally different class of spacecraft. Engineered to survive the harshest radiation environments and to fully capitalize on today’s and tomorrow’s massive rockets, K2 satellites deliver unmatched capability at constellation scale and across multiple orbits.
With multiple launches planned through 2026 and 2027, we're Building Bigger to develop the solar system and become a Kardashev Type II (K2) civilization. If you are a motivated individual who thrives in a fast-paced environment and you're excited about contributing to the success of a groundbreaking Series C space startup, we’d love for you to apply.

The software team at K2 is building our stack primarily in Rust because we believe modern programming languages should be fun, as well as correct. We see Rust as a key enabling technology that allows us to be more effective as software engineers across the entire stack whether that is contributing to the GNC algorithms, application software on flight computers, embedded software on microcontrollers, and many things in-between.

In your first year you will implement larger software systems and begin verifying your code using both software and hardware in the loop simulators. In your first two years you will operate your code on multiple spacecraft, demonstrating robust performance in demanding missions.

Author drivers for microcontroller peripherals and external sensors.
Create and utilize robust tools to allow for rapid deployment of quality code
Perform data analysis and anomaly investigation to identify and resolve software bugs
Support integration and testing of the spacecraft subsystems
Build and maintain infrastructure to increase reliability when developing and testing software

Bachelor's degree in computer science, computer engineering, electrical engineering, math, or a STEM discipline or 3+ years of professional experience in software engineering
Development experience in Rust
Nice to Have
Experience with spacecraft flight software development
Fluency with Linux systems programming and driver development
Experience with continuous integration and continuous delivery systems
Experience working with hard real-time embedded systems (bare-metal or RTOS)
Experience authoring no_std systems in Rust
Basic knowledge of electronics, computer architecture, and control systems
Experience developing or working with state machines
Experience with software verification and testing methods
Experience with software and network performance analysis and debugging
Experience working in Rust production environments
Experience with fault tolerant software design and implementation
Experience defining and creating test systems for both hardware-in-the-loop and hardware-out-of-the-loop

At Miter, we’re on a mission to help construction contractors build with confidence. If we’re successful, we’ll make it easier and faster to build critical physical infrastructure - roads, bridges, utilities, data centers, housing, etc.
For decades, construction and field services contractors have had to run their businesses on outdated software: clunky, on-premise systems created in the 1980s and 1990s.
That’s where Miter comes in. We’re using AI and embedded payments to rebuild the core HR, finance, and operations systems that underpin our physical economy. Using Miter, contractors like Marathon Electrical, W.J. O’Neil, and Truebeck Construction are building stronger teams, controlling job costs, and accelerating jobsite execution.
This idea is resonating. Since we launched in 2021, we’ve grown to thousands of customers and tens of millions in ARR, making us one of the fastest growing vertical software companies ever. To double-down on our momentum, we’ve raised $50M+ from top investors (Bessemer, Coatue, and Battery) who share our belief that we’re just getting started.
About The Team And How We Work
Building the OS for the built world is no small feat. We’ll need to ship a LOT of high quality code in the coming years, and to do so, we’re building an engineering culture centered around craft, ownership, and collaboration. >25% of our engineers and product managers are ex-founders, and we hire for slope, not intercept. No rules…rules: Many engineering teams design processes and rules around the lowest common denominator. Not us! We trust brilliant engineers to deliver magical customer outcomes and introduce processes and rules only when necessary.

Lean and AI-native: AI is turning 10x engineers into 100x engineers. We believe lean, talent-dense, AI-native teams will outship much larger teams with less talent density.
Blueprints and building blocks: One of our core Miter values is “build the blueprint”. Writing things down clarifies our thinking and aligns our teams. This also applies to building fundamental building blocks and abstractions that make developers’ lives easier.
We feel our customers’ pain and celebrate their success: We encourage engineers to build direct relationships with customers, feel their pain, and celebrate their success. We love fast feedback loops.
We’re meritocratic: We value results and hard work. We reward engineers who consistently ship and deliver for customers with increased scope and compensation.

About The Role
We're looking for a Forward Deployed Engineer to own solution design and implementation for our Identity Resolution (IDR) product. This role is a blend of data analytics and data engineering, and is an opportunity to work directly with data, marketing, and executive teams at household-name companies. You'll spend time working with the customer to learn about their data architecture, reason about how Hightouch can accomplish their goals, set up deployments, and debug issues.
This role is hands on and technical. You’ll become intimately familiar with our customers’ data and business goals. This expertise frequently leads to us advising executives at Fortune 500 companies on their long term data strategy. You'll spend time helping customers decide how their global identity spines should be configured, you'll set up implementations for them, and you'll debug inevitable issues with real data. You'll work closely with Sales Engineering on pre-sales deals and with Customer Support Engineering and Technical Account Management on post-sales implementations—serving as the subject matter expert for data engineering and analytics across the customer lifecycle.
You'll work with coding agents as a default: the SQL, schema spelunking, and internal tooling in this role gets built with agents - and you’ll help grow our repository of skills and best practices so we all get faster.
About Hightouch Identity Resolution (IDR)
Imagine you're a sprawling enterprise business with 20+ brands. Each brand collects different data elements from each of their customers and joins using different identifiers. Hightouch IDR can look across the customer data stored in each brand and provide a golden source of truth using all the available data, while obeying any regulatory restrictions that prevent data sharing. The product is highly configurable, and so no two customer data architectures are the same.
What You'll Do
Solution Architecture & Implementation Consulting
Work backwards from end goals: Customers ultimately don't care about IDR itself, but about the use cases that a good identity spine powers. You’ll pair with an architect to work backwards from the customer’s use cases to a set of IDR rules and a data model that enables those use cases
Assess fit and feasibility: During pre-sales, understand the customer’s data landscape and maturity, assessing how much work will be needed to get their data ready for IDR. Understand the rules of any current solutions (e.g., Reltio, Amperity, Segment, MDM tools) and identify, flag, and create workarounds for any gaps.
Technical Support & Debugging
Debug customer issues end-to-end: Investigate perceived issues and discrepancies in identity such as missing datapoints and over-merging scenarios. Most debugging involves writing SQL against customer warehouses and reading server logs.
Explain IDR behavior to customers: Help customers understand how warehouse-native identity resolution works and detailed nuances of how it processes data incrementally or how to utilize its outcome tables.
Surface product gaps: When you see the same issue repeatedly (e.g., no retroactive data removal, insufficient observability into profile changes, inability to reset incremental processing watermarks), flag and advocate for fixes.
What We're Looking For
You direct agents, you don't just prompt them. You'll point them at warehouses with undocumented tables and no reliable dictionary, and you'll be the last judgment before what they build ships to millions of people. You reach for an agent before a blank editor, but you scrutinize every line before it goes out.
SQL Fluency: Anyone can generate a thousand lines of SQL now. You're hired because you can read them and find the join that's wrong. Fluent in Snowflake, Databricks or BigQuery, with query performance and warehouse cost as things you think about unprompted.
Systems thinking: You can reason about how identity graphs behave at scale, understand trade-offs between different architecture choices, and anticipate downstream consequences of design decisions.
Consultative communication: You can run a discovery call, ask the right questions to understand requirements, and explain technical trade-offs to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Systematic debugging mindset: You naturally form hypotheses, test them, and document findings. When you see "missing data," you think through timestamps, model definitions, and PK validity before jumping to conclusions.
2-4 years in an analytics engineering, solutions engineering, forward-deployed engineering, or implementation role—ideally at a data infrastructure, CDP, or B2B SaaS company.

Experience with identity resolution, MDM, or CDP products (Segment, Amperity, Reltio, LiveRamp)
Familiarity with graph data structures and entity resolution algorithms

Creators bring to life games, companions that remember and grow with them, learning experiences that adapt like a great tutor, and social worlds built with friends. The platform also powers our research with data no video dataset contains: millions of creators prompting and refining gives us paired data of human intent and the worlds that fulfill it, and every play session produces ground-truth, action-labeled interaction data at scale. All of it flows back into our models, and research ships to real players in days, spinning a flywheel no one else can build.

You'll dig into real creator sessions to find where generation breaks down, build the evals that tell us whether a change actually helped, and design the agentic systems behind the next version of creation on the platform. https://www.linkedin.com/jobs/view/44716.description_preview:
About The Team
We build the cloud-native software that thousands of rental businesses around the world run on every day — the rental management platform and the e-commerce suite that sits on top of it.
This role is how we bring new engineers into that work. You'll start where the whole system is visible: verifying, breaking, and instrumenting the product before a customer ever sees it. That vantage point is one of the fastest ways there is to learn a large codebase and a complicated domain at the same time. And you'll be writing code from your first sprint — reading it, fixing it, shipping it alongside the developers, not filing tickets over a wall at them.
We built this role deliberately as an entry point for people early in their engineering careers.
What you'll do
Write code from your first sprint
Write and maintain automated tests in the same repositories and the same languages as the product — JavaScript and TypeScript against our Angular front ends and Node/NestJS services, PHP where our longer-standing surfaces live
Read the codebase to work out why something broke, not just that it broke
Fix low-risk defects yourself and take them through code review like any other engineer
Build the small internal tools and scripts that make the team's testing and release process faster
Take on scoped product work under a mentor's review as you ramp
Do the quality work that teaches you the system
Verify new features and fixes across our web and desktop products, and write bug reports a developer can act on immediately
Build and maintain test plans for new features alongside senior engineers
Run regression passes so a new release doesn't break what already worked
Partner with developers and product managers to understand requirements and flag gaps early
Take part in release readiness reviews
What you bring
You can write and read code in at least one language. We care that you can build something and explain the choices you made — not which stack you learned on.
Something we can look at: a capstone, a bootcamp project, a personal project, a GitHub profile, or work from a previous role
A foundation in software development or testing, through a degree, a coding bootcamp, a self-taught path, an internship, or early professional experience
Strong written communication — your bug reports and your commit messages both tell the whole story
Curiosity about how systems break, and the patience to chase an edge case down to its root cause
A working understanding of the software development lifecycle and where quality sits in it
Preferred, not required: exposure to Playwright, Selenium, Cypress or similar; SQL; REST APIs; Azure DevOps or Jira; SaaS products
Who this role is for. You might be arriving from a CS degree, a coding bootcamp, a self-taught path, the military, or a completely different career. You might already work at Point of Rental in support, implementation, or professional services and want to move into engineering — if you know the rental business cold, you already have the half of this job that takes longest to teach. All of those are the point of this role.
How you'll grow
The path from this role is to Full Stack Engineer. That's the destination, and the role is built to get you there.
Start here. Learn the product and the domain. Own exploratory and release testing. Get fluent in our codebase, our tooling, and how we ship.
Then. Write automated tests in the product repositories. Fix defects and take your code through review. Build the internal tooling your team runs on.
Then. Take scoped feature work under mentorship — front end, services, and data — until you're carrying it on your own.
You'll have a named mentor, regular one-on-ones, code review used as a teaching tool, and dedicated learning time every week. We promote on demonstrated ability rather than on a calendar, but the destination is written down and your manager's job is to get you to it.
Why Point of Rental
Point of Rental is the global leader in rental software. The code you write here shows up in equipment yards, event companies, and job sites on six continents, in the hands of people who notice immediately when something is wrong.
You'll be an engineer from day one — in the repositories, in code review, in the room with the developers and product managers shipping the product. We opened this role because we would rather build engineers than only buy them.

About The Opportunity
We're looking for a Support Engineer to be the first technical line of defense behind our customer-facing team. When a client reports that something looks wrong - a chart that wasn't processed, a code that didn't appear, an integration that stopped sending data, an output that doesn't match what the clinician documented - you are the person who figures out what actually happened, why, and what it would take to fix it.
This is not a customer-facing role. Our Technical Success Managers own the client relationship and deliver outcomes to customers. You own the investigation behind them: reproducing the issue, tracing it to a root cause in data, logs, configuration, or code, resolving what you can directly, and handing Engineering a well-scoped diagnosis and proposed fix for what you can't. Your work is what lets our customer team give clients fast, accurate answers - and what protects our engineers' time for building.

Own the Loop Internally: Track every open issue from intake to resolution. Follow up with Engineering, confirm fixes in production, and tell the customer team when it's safe to close the loop with the client.
Build the Knowledge Base: Turn every investigation into reusable knowledge - runbooks, known-issue write-ups, diagnostic queries, and triage guides - so the same question takes minutes, not hours, the next time, and so the customer team can self-serve more over time.

Customer experience is at the heart of all we do at Amazon, as we strive to be Earth's most customer-centric company. Within CS, Human in the Loop (HITL) engineering brings human judgment into AI-handled conversations in real time, across every use case, channel, and marketplace where automation reaches its limit. We build the systems that predict when a bot is about to fail. We summarize live conversation context so a Customer Service Associate can decide in seconds, and we execute that decision back into the conversation while the customer is still in it, with no transfer and nothing to re-explain. Every intervention also becomes training data for the next contact like it, so the case that needed a human this time is one automation can handle on its own the next. That is why HITL compounds instead of plateauing.
We are looking for a Software Development Engineer to help build that platform and shape the architecture behind it. Today HITL runs tens of thousands of customer contacts every week across four use cases in the US, UK, and Canada. What stands between us and ten times that is the architecture itself. Core logic is spread across several services, each new use case takes about six weeks to launch, and tight coupling to our current bot stack blocks entire product lines where human judgment would matter most. You will be a significant contributor to fixing that. You will help design and build HITL as a standalone platform, shape the contracts that let any bot in CS request human judgment, and make the real-time path fast and reliable enough that a customer sitting in a live conversation never knows a human was involved.

Orchestration across multiple customer service systems with no single owner
LLM inference inside a conversation a customer is waiting in
Triggering logic that has to be right at the moment it fires, not just in aggregate
A keep-alive mechanism that will not survive our next scale-up
Feedback pipelines that turn every associate decision into training data worth learning from.

Own the design and delivery of major HITL components, from technical design through production launch and ongoing operation.

Partner with applied scientists to productionize ML and generative AI components, including context summarization and proactive questioning, and own the serving path, evaluation harness, and fallback behavior.

Partner with product managers, science, and dependent teams to turn ambiguous customer experience problems into scoped technical plans, and push back when requirements do not survive contact with the architecture.
Contribute to roadmap and planning, including flagging the technical investments the team should make before they turn into blockers.

Some days are heads-down implementation on a service in the live contact path. Others are a design review where you are defending a contract decision that partner teams will build against, or a production investigation where a latency regression is something customers are feeling right now. You will balance the current use-case launch against the platform work that makes the next ten cheap, and you will help decide where that line sits. You will spend real time with applied scientists making models production-viable, and real time with the engineers around you making their designs better.

About Rare Candy
Rare Candy is revolutionizing the $25 billion trading-card industry as the “friendly local game shop” in the palm of your hands. Collectors use our AI-powered card scanner, open their favorite chase cards with Instapacks, and keep track of them with our data-rich collection tools which showcases Pokémon, MTG, Lorcana, One Piece, and more. We've hit 10x revenue growth over the last 6 months, the business is profitable, and we're building the team to take this from a great product to a category-defining one.
We're a 10-person product team moving fast and looking for the next set of TCG-obsessed rock stars to join our team.
The Role
We’re hiring a mid-level Web Engineer to build the web experiences collectors use to discover products, manage their collections, shop drops, and open Instapacks.
You’ll work closely with the CTO and product, design, and engineering teams to take features from idea to production. This is a hands-on product engineering role for someone comfortable building modern web applications who can own a feature, make thoughtful technical decisions, and deliver a polished experience.
You won’t be handed endless tickets in a giant backlog. You’ll help shape solutions, work through tradeoffs, and take responsibility for how your features perform once they’re in collectors’ hands.
If you love trading cards or collector communities and want meaningful ownership at a fast-moving startup, this is a role for you.
What Success Looks Like
First 30 days: You get the web app running locally, understand the core product flows and frontend architecture, and ship your first meaningful improvements.
By day 90: You’re independently delivering well-scoped web features. You can clarify requirements, collaborate with design and backend engineers, implement the experience, test it, and verify it in production.
By the end of year one: You own important areas of the web product. You’ve shipped meaningful improvements to the collector experience, raised the bar for performance and usability, and made the codebase easier for the team to build on.
What You'll Do
Build and improve responsive web experiences across Rare Candy’s collector-facing product.
Develop maintainable interfaces using React, TypeScript, and modern web tooling.
Integrate with GraphQL APIs and collaborate with backend engineers on data requirements and API contracts.
Own features from technical planning through implementation, testing, rollout, and follow-up improvements.
Build reusable components and consistent interaction patterns that help the team ship faster.
Make experiences work well across devices and browsers, with attention to accessibility, loading states, error handling, and performance.
Investigate production bugs and address the underlying causes.
Work closely with product and design to balance user needs, technical constraints, and delivery timelines.
Contribute thoughtful code reviews and communicate clearly about progress, tradeoffs, and blockers.
A Day in Your Life at Rare Candy
You start the morning reviewing feedback on a recently shipped feature and checking how it’s performing for collectors.
Mid-morning, you’re working with design and a backend engineer to scope a new collection browsing experience, thinking through the API, filtering behavior, and mobile layout.
After lunch, you’re building the interface, connecting it to live data, and handling loading, empty, and error states. You catch a slow interaction and track it down before opening your PR.
Later in the day, you’re in a product discussion about an upcoming drop, bringing both your web engineering perspective and your own TCG fluency to the conversation.
You close the day by reviewing a teammate’s code and sharing your own PR with a clear summary, screenshots, and testing notes.
You Might Be a Fit If
You have around 3–5 years of web engineering experience and have shipped meaningful features in production.
You’re comfortable building with React and TypeScript and have strong fundamentals in JavaScript, HTML, and CSS.
You can take a feature from a product brief or design through implementation and release without needing every step spelled out.
You’ve worked with GraphQL or REST APIs and understand data fetching, caching, and client-side state management.
You know how to build responsive, accessible interfaces and care about the details that make a web experience feel good.
You can reason through component design, rendering behavior, and performance tradeoffs without overcomplicating the solution.
You write useful tests and know how to debug issues across the browser, network requests, and API responses.
You communicate technical tradeoffs clearly and work well with designers, product partners, and other engineers.
You’re comfortable in a fast-moving startup where priorities can shift and you’re expected to help find the path forward.
You know the trading-card or collector world. You collect, play, rip packs, follow the market, or have real fluency in a similar collectible space.
What You'll Need to Thrive Here
You’re expected to take ownership of your role at Rare Candy and drive your own growth. That doesn’t mean doing it alone. You’ll have support, context, and mentorship along the way.
The systems are still evolving, the team is small, and your work will matter immediately. You'll need to be curious, detail-oriented, and comfortable learning by doing.
If you like to build internal tools, solve operational issues, and the idea of building tools you would actually want to use yourself, you'll do great here.
Why Join Us Now
Work on features collectors actually care about and are using everyday.
Get real ownership early in your career while learning directly from experienced engineering leadership.
Join a high-trust, low-ego team that ships fast, celebrates wins, and care

We're hiring a Fullstack Developer to help build the operations toolchain we use every day to manage our warehouse, inventory, and managing our Instapacks business.
You'll work closely with the CTO and engineering team to ship new tools and features for our operations team. This is a hands-on product engineering role for someone who loves solving logistic problems, has a background in GO and React, and wants to grow quickly inside a fast-moving startup.
You won't be handed endless tickets in a giant backlog. You'll work on real problems, learn from phenomenal backend engineers, and see your work go directly into the hands of passionate collectors.
If you love trading cards or collector communities, this is a role for you.

You get the various ops tools running locally, understand the core problems, and ship your first meaningful fixes or small features.
By day 90:
You're regularly shipping features for our Ops team with support from the CTO and principal engineer. You can take a well-scoped feature or improvement, ask the right questions, implement it cleanly, test it, and get it into the team's hands.

Build and improve our Ops toolchain to help support our entire Warehouse and Logistics team.
Fix bugs, improve bottlenecks, and raise the quality bar for Ops toolchain.
Work closely with ops and engineering to increase efficiency to hard problems.
Learn quickly, ask good questions, and communicate clearly when something is blocked, unclear, or ready for review.

You start the morning checking in with the warehouse team and reviewing feedback on a feature you shipped yesterday.
Mid-morning, you're pairing with other engineers on making improvements on various backend services.
After lunch, you're tightening up a dashboard, fixing an edge case, and testing the flow against real time operations.
Later in the day, you're in an operations discussion about how we want to launch a new game for Instapacks and how our toolchain needs to support it.
You close the day by opening a PR with a clear summary, and a note about what still needs review.

Work on features collectors actually care about and are using everyday.

ContractorHUB is building the AI-native operating system for home service businesses. We’re a small, fast-moving team building an ambitious product and rethinking how software gets developed along the way.

This role will define & own the standard for what “ready to ship” means at ContractorHUB.
The role
We’re looking for a Product Quality Engineer to own quality across the ContractorHUB platform.
This is an engineering role, not a traditional manual QA position. You’ll work directly in our Laravel/PHP codebase, investigate and fix issues, submit code, build automated testing, and help establish the systems and standards we use to confidently ship product.
You’ll also help us rethink QA for an AI-forward development environment. We want someone who is comfortable using AI throughout their own work and interested in finding better ways to automate testing, identify problems earlier, and improve the reliability of an increasingly fast development cycle.
What you'll do
Own product quality and help define what “done” looks like before features ship
Test new features across functionality, integrations, APIs, permissions, multi-tenant environments, browsers, and devices
Investigate bugs down to the code level, identify root causes, and submit fixes
Build and maintain automated tests that improve coverage and reduce regression risk
Use AI and automation to make testing faster, more thorough, and more scalable
Develop repeatable QA and release-readiness processes as our engineering organization grows
Work closely with Product and Engineering to identify risks earlier in the development process
Validate AI-powered product experiences, including behavior that isn't always deterministic
Help us move quickly without accepting “we'll fix it later” as the standard

You’re a software engineer who gets upset when something doesn't work the way it should
You have hands-on experience with PHP/Laravel or a background that will allow you to get productive in the stack quickly
You have experience with automated testing and understand when manual testing still matters
You can trace an issue from what a customer sees all the way back to what is happening in the code
You’re comfortable fixing problems yourself rather than simply documenting and handing them off
You’re excited about AI-assisted software development and already adopting these modern development approaches
You’re thorough without becoming a bottleneck
You can manage your own priorities and keep pushing until the work is actually finished
You want meaningful ownership without needing a management title

Our development process is highly AI-forward. We use AI throughout engineering, from writing and reviewing code to testing, troubleshooting, and accelerating development.
That lets a small team move incredibly quickly. It also raises the bar for how we think about quality—we don't mail it in. We need to ensure the highest standard of quality for our customers.
You’ll have the opportunity to help build that system with us: deciding where automation belongs, where human judgment matters, and how we create enough confidence in our product to keep increasing the speed at which we build.
You’ll report directly to Matt Parks, Founder & Chief Product & Innovation Officer, and work closely with the rest of our Product and Engineering team.

Competitive compensation based on experience
Performance bonus opportunities
Health and dental benefits
Internet and phone stipend
Equity options
Remote-first team
To apply
We care about what you can do.
Tell us about something you’ve built, fixed, tested, or improved that demonstrates how you think as an engineer. We’re especially interested in examples where you found a problem others missed, built a better way to prevent it from happening again, or used AI and automation to improve how software gets shipped. About Production Engineering
Production Engineering is Ramp's infrastructure ownership layer. We exist to make Ramp faster, more reliable, and more scalable — and we do that by being embedded in the problems, not adjacent to them.
A few things that define how we operate:
One team, one company, one objective. There is no "infra team" and "product team" — there is Ramp. We share the company's goals as our own. When a product team struggles with reliability or scalability, that is our struggle.
If reliability or scalability is at risk, we own it. We don't wait to be invited, and we don't ask whose code it is. If a system is slow, if it breaks, if it won't scale — that's ours to lead, regardless of where it lives in the stack.
We go first, and we go fast. When the path isn't obvious, we don't wait for someone else to find it. We move with urgency, propose the solution, align the stakeholders, and stay in until it's done — not until our ticket is closed.
We lead the way. We find the next problem before it finds us. And when we solve it, we don't just fix it for ourselves — the patterns and standards we establish become the foundation the rest of Ramp builds on. That's not a side effect of the job; it's the job.
We stay calibrated. Speed means nothing if we're moving in the wrong direction. We regularly stop and ask honestly whether what we're working on is still the highest-leverage thing we could be doing — the discipline that makes sure our effort compounds toward what actually matters.
You cannot build the future of finance on shaky infrastructure.

Production Engineering is organized into teams — but we think about teams differently. Teams are mutable. We build them around what needs to be done, not around what we need to do given the teams we already have. The structure below reflects our current priorities; it will evolve as Ramp does.

Compute — the foundation everything runs on: container orchestration, networking, load balancing, edge infrastructure, and the deployment systems that get code from engineers' laptops to production reliably and at scale
Storage — databases, caching, object storage, and the data infrastructure that underpins everything

Embedded Systems Emulation Engineer
to join our multidisciplinary team of researchers and engineers developing cutting-edge technologies with significant and immediate impact on our national security. Join the team bringing advanced autonomy to the built world
At Bedrock, we're moving AI out of the lab and into the real world. Our team includes veterans who helped launch Waymo, scaled Segment to a $3.2B acquisition, and grew Uber Freight to $5B in revenue. Today, we're deploying autonomous systems on heavy construction equipment across the country, improving safety on job sites and accelerating schedules on critical infrastructure projects.
We're not here debating the future of AI. We're deploying it in the real world. In just two years, we've raised $350M and achieved the first fully autonomous excavator deployments in construction.
This is where algorithms meet steel-toed boots. You'll work alongside construction veterans and world-class engineers to solve physical-world problems that simulations can't touch. If you're ready to do meaningful work on hard problems, we'd love to have you join us.
We’re looking for a
Software Engineer
to develop the state-estimation systems that allow autonomous machines to understand their position, orientation, motion, and configuration. You’ll build production software that combines data from GNSS, IMUs, lidar, machine sensors, and other sources in rugged environments the machines themselves are actively reshaping.
Accurate state estimation is essential to both safety and performance. Your work will help our machines operate precisely, recognize when sensor data or estimates are unreliable, and respond safely when inputs are delayed, degraded, or unavailable.
Depending on your background, you may focus on real-time sensor fusion, estimator reliability, lidar-based estimation, offline optimization, or calibration. This is a hands-on role spanning algorithm design, production software, data analysis, and testing on real machines.
What You’ll Do
Design, implement, and deploy state-estimation and localization algorithms for autonomous construction machines
Combine GNSS, IMU, lidar, and machine-sensor data into accurate, real-time estimates of machine position, motion, and configuration
Improve reliability through sensor monitoring, consistency checks, fault detection, trustworthy confidence estimates, redundancy, and graceful degradation
Handle measurements that arrive late, out of order, intermittently, or not at all
Build ground-truth systems, offline reference estimators, metrics, and regression tests that measure performance and expose failures
Work on related problems such as sensor calibration, clock synchronization, lidar-based arm estimation, and joint offline estimation
Diagnose issues using field data, recorded-data replay, and simulation, then test improvements on physical machines
Collaborate with controls, perception, safety, hardware, and systems teams to improve the performance of the complete autonomy system
What We're Looking For
4+ years of professional engineering or applied research experience in state estimation, localization, navigation, SLAM, or sensor fusion
Strong foundations in probabilistic estimation, linear algebra, 3D geometry, and numerical methods
Hands-on experience with one or more of GNSS/INS fusion, Kalman filtering, factor graphs, lidar or visual odometry, point-cloud registration, or sensor calibration
Strong production software skills in Rust or modern C++. Our production stack is primarily Rust, and we will support experienced C++ engineers as they ramp up
Experience measuring estimator performance using ground truth, recorded data, simulation, and real-world testing
Strong debugging and data-analysis skills, including the ability to investigate problems across algorithms, software, sensors, and hardware
A degree in Robotics, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Applied Mathematics, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience
Ways To Stand Out
Experience deploying state-estimation systems on autonomous vehicles, robots, or embedded platforms
Experience with estimator monitoring, uncertainty, fault detection, redundancy, or safety-relevant systems
Experience with nonlinear optimization, factor graphs, or smoothing
Deep knowledge of GNSS, inertial sensing, lidar, sensor timing, calibration, and real-world failure modes
Experience with lidar localization, ICP, continuous-time estimation, or articulated-machine estimation
Experience building offline reference estimators or independent ground-truth systems
Production experience with Rust
Familiarity with construction, mining, agricultural, or other heavy industrial machines
Other Special Aspects Of The Role
Based in San Francisco with the ability to be onsite at our SF office 3 day a week

Job Description
Hearst Journalism Fellowship Program, Newsroom AI Development
The
Hearst Fellowship for Newsroom AI Development
is a one-year program focused on building tools for journalists and experiences for readers with the cutting-edge technology. The successful candidate will embed on the DevHub, Hearst’s San Francisco-based editorial innovation team, and they will work on AI-assisted projects, tools and news products with our core product and engineering teams and our top metro newsrooms: San Francisco Chronicle, Houston Chronicle, Dallas Morning News, Austin American-Statesman, San Antonio Express-News, (Albany) Times Union and our Hearst Connecticut newsrooms.
Fellows will receive training, mentorship and real-world experience alongside top journalist-programmers who build interactive experiences and automation tools focused on building connections to the local communities we cover.
Hearst Fellows are full-time employees with competitive salary and benefits, including health insurance, relocation allowance and a housing stipend.
What The DevHub Does
The Hearst DevHub is a team of editorial engineers, AI developers, data journalists, interactive designers and content strategists who collaborate with local newsrooms to create best-in-class digital experiences. We make things like election results pages, AI tools, searchable databases, severe weather trackers, elegantly designed alternative story forms and whatever else you can dream up. You can learn more about the DevHub here .
What This Fellowship Could Mean For Your Future
Our goal for the program is for Fellows to earn full-time employment at the end of the yearlong term. We want to train our next builders, and then continue supporting them as they grow into our future leaders.
While participation in the program is not a guarantee of future employment, our goal is to recruit candidates who eventually will join our full-time professional staff. All of us here have an investment in your future and in the future of Hearst Newspapers.
What The Successful Candidate Will Do On The DevHub
Create AI tools for newsrooms and experiences for readers that adhere to our strict editorial standards and company policies.
Work with newsrooms on best practices for AI usage.
Enrich existing tools and interactives with fresh approaches to workflows, data analysis and visualization.
Innovate with new technology to benefit journalists and the communities we cover.
Hearst Fellowships jump-start great journalism careers
The experience you gain as a Hearst Fellow is the start of a strong foundation for your journalism career. Our objective is to recruit, train and retain journalists who have experience with AI, data journalism and programming. Candidates should be college graduates with interest, experience or background in journalism and AI.
How Fellows Are Selected
Hearst DevHub team members will conduct multiple interviews and test the top candidates.
If you are offered and accept a position, you will be assigned a mentor, and we’ll help you develop relationships with seasoned professionals throughout Hearst Newspapers and beyond.
Requirements And Information
Please see our Fellows website at https://hearstfellowships.com . In addition, candidates must be willing to relocate to the San Francisco Bay Area and work a hybrid in-office schedule.
To be considered you must submit in all required documents in PDF format:
One-page resume that includes past journalistic experience, academic major and minor, date or expected date of graduation, permanent and current addresses, email, website, and social media addresses (if applicable).
Reference page that includes three work references including titles, email addresses and phone numbers.
Page with links to portfolio or digital work samples.
Deadline to apply for the Fellowship program is Jan. 4, 2027.

Description
Amazon Leo is building a global e-commerce experience for Internet Service Provider (ISP) customers, and we need a Front End Engineer II to help us do it. You will work with React and Next.js to design, build, and ship features that serve customers worldwide. Many of these experiences are built from zero-to-one, so you will regularly move from ambiguous problem to working product. You will own the full software development lifecycle, collaborating with product, marketing, business, and backend engineering partners to deliver accessible, performant interfaces. If you enjoy working with AI-driven development workflows, picking up new frameworks quickly, and turning complex requirements into clean user experiences, this is the role for you.
Export Control Requirement
Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.
Key job responsibilities
Design and build front-end features for the Amazon Leo e-commerce platform using React and Next.js, taking projects from concept through deployment and ongoing operation.
Collaborate with product managers, UX designers, marketing, and backend commerce service teams to translate customer and business needs into accessible, scalable solutions that work across devices and browsers.
Leverage agentic development workflows and generative AI tools to accelerate feature delivery, and identify opportunities to improve infrastructure using AWS native services.
Participate actively in code reviews, providing constructive feedback to teammates while coaching others on front-end best practices, UI design patterns, and maintainable coding standards.
Write clear documentation for your team's software and train new team members on how it is constructed, tested, and operated.
A day in the life
You might start your morning reviewing a pull request from a teammate, suggesting improvements to a React component's accessibility and performance. After standup, you pick up a new feature that doesn't have a clear precedent yet, sketching out an approach with your product manager before writing code. In the afternoon, you pair with a designer to refine interaction details for an upcoming launch, then dig into an operational metric that looks off, tracing it to a rendering edge case you fix before it reaches customers.

We are part of the Leo Commerce engineering organization at Amazon, building the e-commerce experience for a global ISP customer base. Our team works closely with backend commerce services, product, marketing, and business partners to launch new experiences from scratch. 1+ years of computer science fundamentals (object-oriented design, data structures, algorithm design, problem solving and complexity analysis) experience
Experience using JavaScript frameworks such as angular and react

1+ years of agile software development methodology experience
Experience with common front-end technologies such as HTML, CSS, JS, TypeScript, and Node

About Us
MintMCP helps companies put agents to work safely. We exist to help companies do more of their work with agents, and we build the infrastructure that makes a company's own work runnable by them. That has to start from trust. Our first product is an MCP gateway that gives those agents governed access to company data and tools.
Before agents can touch Slack, GitHub, Jira, Snowflake, internal databases, or production systems, you need to know what they can reach, what they did, and why they were allowed to do it. Most people carry far more permissions than any single task needs. If an agent uses your token directly, it inherits all of them. MintMCP scopes that access down to exactly what an agent needs to do its job and captures the data flows and audit logs security teams need. From there we are building the rest of the agent stack: connectors, monitoring, sandboxing, long-running agents, and memory, with the goal of becoming the system a company's work runs on.
We work in person in the San Francisco Bay Area. The structure is flat and the market moves fast, so you have a lot of latitude over what you work on and how.
We are AI-native. Everyone uses Claude and Codex every day, and we have more agents than employees. They run in Slack alongside the team and handle sales, marketing, deal ops, and engineering on the same gateway we sell to customers, and we are building an entire company operating system around them.
Since launching in February 2026, we have grown to 50+ paying customers, with strong inbound demand. Customers include Coursera, Arlo, and Braze. We are backed by Cowboy Ventures and Coatue, with angels including Frederic Kerrest (Okta), Michael Grinich (WorkOS), Andrej Karpathy, Jeff Dean, and Scott Belsky. The Job
You will own features end to end, from conception to production, across our gateway infrastructure, enterprise deployments, and agentic systems. The work leans backend and infra, but nothing is off limits: when the product needs a better UI you build it, and when a connector breaks during a security review you fix it.
Claude and Codex are your primary working environment, and you use a fleet of agents to move faster than a team this size has any right to. Agents write much of the code and review PRs, so your real job is the judgment they cannot make: shaping the problem, making architecture, product, and UX calls, hardening enterprise paths, designing connectors, protecting security-sensitive surfaces, and catching generated code that is quietly wrong. Roles are blurred and we ship within hours, and you will learn directly from the founders and from customers.
We hire across levels, from strong early-career builders to seasoned engineers, and we set level and pay to match. What matters most is judgment, range, and how fast you ship.
About You
You are a builder with a track record of shipping to real users, whether that is a product, an internal tool, an open-source project, or a serious side project. You ship, then iterate, without waiting for specs or approvals.
You have strong fundamentals and learn fast. How quickly you pick things up matters as much as years of experience.
You care about product value and customer needs over technical purity.
You take infra seriously. You think about blast radius, trust boundaries, and what happens when your code is in the path of every customer's agents.
You can read unfamiliar code, reason from first principles, and explain your tradeoffs.
You are comfortable across the stack (TypeScript, Python, CockroachDB), or you pick up new languages, protocols, and domains fast.
You are excited to build with agents, and to learn when they help and when they hide a problem.
You already build with AI every day and want room to move without heavy process.

Design sensibility: engineers who care about design, designers who think about infrastructure.

Document design decisions and build patterns from your bespoke customer engagements to feed our use case library and core product roadmap.

Qumulo serves everything from a hospital's medical imaging archive to an animation studio's render farm in an environment where 99% correct doesn’t cut it.
About the Role:
Joining us for our Summer 2027 internship program, you'd learn and work across our distributed storage engine and the services that help customers store, manage, and protect their data, under the guidance of experienced senior engineers.
This includes a fault-tolerant block layer that erasure-codes and distributes data beneath the file system, a transactional file system where aggregates roll up as they change so a query across billions of files answers in real time instead of walking a tree, and that same machinery drives quotas, capacity trends, snapshot policy, multiple access protocols, plus replication and backup - all running in userspace.
All of which makes Qumulo a distributed operating system problem: scheduling, memory hierarchy, protection, and concurrency. We're AI-forward and specific about what that means. You will learn to use agents to help write code while developing your engineering judgment to ensure every design decision is correct, because nothing ships that isn't right.
Why intern at Qumulo:
Qumulo blends the flexibility of a startup with the security of a mature and profitable organization. Here you’ll work closely with a small team of smart, capable engineers who will serve as your mentors. Opinions are expected, disagreement is normal, and you'll get hands-on experience taking projects from ideation to release. We value quality, correctness, and performance. Our architecture, protocols, and patents are public, so you can read how most of this works before you talk to us - and we’re small enough that the work you do during your internship will actually show up in the product.
As a Software Engineering Intern at Qumulo, you will:
Collaborate with team members on design, code reviews, and pair programming
Collaborate with team members and area leads on architecture and design of new/updated features
Work directly with a team on core product features; not on a siloed intern project
Contribute to feature development and testing using C, Rust and Python
Define and implement customer-facing features and internal improvements
Help debug and fix test failures and product or service issues
What we're looking for:
Ability to write well-factored and well-tested code
Strong grasp of algorithms and data structures, with some experience in distributed systems, database concepts, concurrent programming, or operating systems concepts
At least one class, internship or personal project using C, C++, Rust, Java, or Go
Willingness to work collaboratively with a team to solve complex problems
Ability to reside in Seattle for the duration of your internship
Pursuing a BS or BA in Computer Science or Computer Engineering or equivalent experience, available for a full-time internship during Winter, Spring, or Summer 2027
Must be authorized to work in the United States. We are unable to provide visa sponsorship or transfer. This role is hybrid, based at our downtown Seattle HQ, targeting 3 days a week in-office.
The base pay for this intern role is USD $100,000 annual base salary (prorated to $1,900 per week for the duration of your internship), plus relocation, travel, and local transit support as applicable.
About Qumulo:
Built for the most demanding enterprise workloads, from AI and HPC simulations to Splunk Observability, genomics and PACS medical imaging, geospatial datasets, media editing and rendering, and video surveillance, Qumulo unlocks the full power of an organization’s information. Our platform unifies file and object storage across data centers, edge, and public clouds, enabling efficient, accelerated computing and extending the reach of data unbound by protocol or transport limitations.
With more than 1,100 customers and exabytes of data under management, Qumulo powers mission-critical workloads anywhere real-time access to massive file datasets is non-negotiable. Qumulo delivers radical simplicity, hardware freedom, exceptional customer support, and a true hybrid-cloud architecture.
Our Values:
At Qumulo, we are building an open and collaborative culture where people can do their best work with customers as our magnetic field. We act as owners, we share by default, we are data driven and experimental and as an inclusive workplace, we encourage and celebrate multiple points of view. As part of our culture we believe diversity drives innovation.

Join Axon and be a Force for Good.
At Axon, we’re on a mission to Protect Life. We’re explorers, pursuing society’s most critical safety and justice issues with our ecosystem of devices and cloud software. This isn't a relationship management role. It's an ownership role. Sharp. Adaptable. Unstoppable. As a Mission Engineer II, you'll work directly alongside public safety agencies to turn real operational challenges into working technical solutions.

Embed with assigned agencies to understand their mission, people, workflows, systems, and priorities.
Develop broad knowledge of the Axon ecosystem and deeper expertise in the products deployed at your agency.
Work with frontline users, technical teams, and agency leadership to uncover operational friction.
Translate customer problems into clear technical requirements and measurable success criteria.
Identify opportunities for AI, automation, data, and Axon capabilities to improve how the agency operates.
Understand what the customer needs—not simply what they initially ask for.

Apply foundational software engineering concepts including APIs, data structures, scripting, testing, debugging, and version control.

Configure and extend capabilities across Axon's technology ecosystem.
Understand when you can solve the problem yourself and when deeper Product or Engineering partnership is required.
Build with Axon—not around it.

Move solutions from discovery into real customer use.
Test and iterate alongside the people who will actually use what you build.
Drive adoption and measure results against agreed success criteria.
Continue improving solutions until they create sustained operational value.
Document successful solutions so they can be maintained, improved, and reused.

Maintain a consistent onsite presence and deep understanding of the agency's Axon environment.
Lean into critical customer needs when your technical context or involvement can materially improve the outcome.
Help quarterback technical alignment around important deployments without replacing the teams responsible for deployment execution.
Serve as a liaison when complex technical issues require coordination beyond standard Support.
Help customers navigate capabilities across products such as Records, Fusus, AI Era, and the broader Axon ecosystem.
Connect the right resources across Product, Engineering, Support, Deployment, Training, Mission Operations, Mission Success, and Sales.
Continuously ask: What are we learning, what could work better, and what could we build so this is easier next time?
Return to the highest-value build opportunities once immediate customer needs are addressed.
Learn in the Field. Improve Axon.
Capture recurring customer needs, workflow patterns, and technical friction.
Share successful builds and lessons across Mission Engineering.
Bring platform limitations and customer insights back to Product and Engineering.
Identify solutions that could be reused by other MEs and agencies.

Foundational software engineering capability and demonstrated experience building technical solutions.
Working knowledge of APIs, scripting/ programming, data, testing, debugging, and modern development practices.
Understanding of AI concepts and practical applications.
Strong technical curiosity and ability to rapidly learn emerging platforms and tools.
Ability to solve ambiguous problems rather than simply execute predefined tasks.
Strong communication skills across technical and non-technical audiences.
Customer-facing mindset and curiosity about how organizations actually operate.

Ability to maintain the onsite presence required by the engagement.

Experience with Python, JavaScript, SQL, REST APIs, cloud platforms, or modern frameworks.
